statement: For fourteen general k-rational point conditions over a characteristic-zero field k, the quadratically enriched count of rational plane quintics is 34520h+18264⟨1⟩ in GW(k), equivalently 52784⟨1⟩+34520⟨−1⟩.

source.location: Definition 2.18 and Theorem 2.19, printed page12; Definitions2.10 and Theorem2.11; combine with arXiv:2502.02569v4 Theorem1.2/Proposition5.3 and the cited exact degree-five N5,W5 values
source.version: arXiv:2309.12586v2 (23 September 2024), with arXiv:2502.02569v4 (30 June 2026); primary PDFs inspected 4 November 2026

scope: Quadratically enriched count of irreducible rational degree-five plane curves through fourteen general k-rational points, over a characteristic-zero field k.
notes:
Explicit deduction, not a quintic table quoted from the paper. For weight-one ends, every arithmetic tropical multiplicity is an integer combination of ⟨1⟩ and ⟨−1⟩. Its rank is the complex multiplicity and its real signature is the Welschinger multiplicity. Consequently the total class is ((N5−W5)/2)h+W5⟨1⟩. Substitute N5=87304 (Fomin–Mikhalkin Figure 1) and W5=18264 (Itenberg–Kharlamov–Shustin printed page2): (87304−18264)/2=34520. The correspondence theorem identifies this class with the algebraic enriched count. The real signature18264 is a signed count and does not assert a sharp unsigned minimum.

The numerical count is associated with the earlier recursion (Kontsevich–Manin for rational curves). Fomin–Mikhalkin’s table remains the inspected verification source; their floor-diagram Theorem 1.6 explicitly restates Brugallé–Mikhalkin. This is not a claim that the individual numerical value was historically first found by the cited recursion.

For the all-k-rational point constraints used here, the underlying enriched correspondence is Jaramillo Puentes–Pauli (arXiv:2309.11706). The later four-author papers explicitly credit that case; their new extension-point results are not needed for this record. Displayed numerical specializations and the rank/signature deduction remain as stated.
